Name: Reporting on efforts to combat sexual harassment and equal employment opportunity violations at city agencies, and to repeal local law number 101 for the year 2018.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to reporting on efforts to combat sexual harassment and equal employment opportunity violations at city agencies, and to repeal local law number 101 for the year 2018, relating to the climate surveys and action plans to combat sexual harassment and equal employment opportunity violations at city agencies

Summary: This bill would require the report on anti-sexual harassment trainings at city agencies from Department of Citywide Administrative Services (DCAS) to provide the number of employees trained, and information about the training. The bill would also require the report on workplace sexual harassment within city agencies to include information about the outcomes of substantiated sexual harassment complaints and the positions of the individuals bringing complaints, anonymized to protect all parties’ privacy. Finally, the bill would repeal Local Law number 101 of 2018 relating to the climate surveys and action plans to combat sexual harassment and equal employment opportunity violations at city agencies; the bill would codify similar requirements regarding climate surveys and action plans and related reporting requirements.

\pard\ltrpar\fi720\sl480\slmult1\qj Section 1. Paragraph 1 of subdivision d of section 815.1 of chapter 35 of the New York city charter, as added by local law number 92 for the year 2018, is amended to read as follows:\par
1. The department of citywide administrative services shall maintain a record of all trainings required pursuant to this section for at least three years. On or before [January 31] \ul March 1\ulnone  of each year the department of citywide administrative services shall report to the mayor and the speaker the results of agency compliance with the requirements of this section. \ul Such reporting shall include the number of employees trained and the number of employees not trained, disaggregated by the following:\par
(a) The type of position of the employee, including, but not limited to, managerial and non-managerial; and\par
(b) The format of the anti-sexual harassment interactive training offered, including, but not limited to, online training and in-person training.\par
\ulnone\'a7 2. Section 3-119.2 of subchapter 1 of chapter 1 of title 3 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by local law number 97 for the year 2018, is amended to read as follows:\par
a. Definitions. For purposes of this section, the following terms have the following meanings:\par
Agency. The term "agency" has the same meaning as such term is defined in section 1150 of the charter and shall include the offices of the borough presidents, the comptroller\ul ,\ulnone  and the public advocate.\par
Department. The term "department" means the department of citywide administrative services.\par
Reporting individual. The term "reporting individual" means a city job or internship applicant, or a current or former employee, intern, independent contractor\ul ,\ulnone  or volunteer who brings forth a report of workplace sexual harassment.\par
Respondent. The term "respondent" means a city job or internship applicant, or a current or former employee, intern, independent contractor\ul ,\ulnone  or volunteer accused of workplace sexual harassment who has entered into the agency's official complaint process.\par
b. \ul Annual report.\ulnone  Each agency shall report to the department complaints of workplace sexual harassment annually. The department shall annually compile complaints of workplace sexual harassment within each agency for the preceding fiscal year and shall annually submit by December 31 to the mayor, the \ul speaker of the\ulnone  council\ul ,\ulnone  and \ul chairperson of the New York city \ulnone commission on human rights, which shall post it on its website, a report containing the following information:\par
1. \ul Information on the complaints filed and determinations by agencies, including:\par
\pard\ltrpar\li720\sl480\slmult1\qj (a)\ulnone  The number of [such] complaints that were filed;\par
\pard\ltrpar\fi720\sl480\slmult1\qj [2.] \ul (b)\ulnone  Of those complaints [in paragraph 1 of this subdivision] \ul filed\ulnone , the number of complaints resolved;\par
[3.] \ul (c)\ulnone  Of those complaints [in paragraph 2 of this subdivision] \ul resolved\ulnone , the number of complaints [substantiated] \ul supported by a preponderance of the evidence\ulnone ;\par
[4.] \ul (d)\ulnone  Of those complaints [in paragraph 2 of this subdivision] \ul filed\ulnone , the number of complaints not [substantiated] \ul supported by a preponderance of the evidence\ulnone ; [and]\par
[5.] \ul (e)\ulnone  The number of complaints in the agency\rquote s official discrimination claim process that were closed because the complaint was withdrawn by the reporting individual prior to a final determination\ul ; and\par
(f) Of those complaints filed and withdrawn, the number of complaints withdrawn before the agency began an investigation as part of such agency\rquote s official discrimination claim process and the number of complaints withdrawn after such investigation began; and\par
2. The number of reporting individuals, disaggregated by each reporting individual\rquote s relationship to the agency, including, but not limited to, job and internship applicant, full-time and part-time employee, intern, employee, independent contractor, and volunteer\ulnone .\ul\par
c. Cumulative report. Each agency shall report to the department the cumulative number of complaints of workplace sexual harassment. On or before December 31, 2027 and on or before December 31 every 4 years thereafter, the department shall compile all complaints of workplace sexual harassment within each agency from the first reporting period required by local law 97 of 2018 until present and shall submit to the mayor, speaker of the council, and chairperson of the New York city commission on human rights, and post on the department\rquote s website, a report containing the following information:\par
1. Information on the complaints filed, including: \par
\pard\ltrpar\li720\sl480\slmult1\qj (a) The number of such complaints that were filed;\par
\pard\ltrpar\fi720\sl480\slmult1\qj (b) Of those complaints filed, the number of complaints resolved in less than 180 days and the number of complaints resolved in 180 days or more;\par
(c) Of those complaints resolved in less than 180 days, the number of complaints supported by a preponderance of the evidence and the number of complaints not supported by a preponderance of the evidence;\par
(d) Of those complaints resolved in 180 days or more, the number of complaints supported by a preponderance of the evidence and the number of complaints not supported by a preponderance of the evidence;\par
(e) The number of complaints in the agency\rquote s official discrimination claim process that were closed because the complaint was withdrawn by the reporting individual prior to a final determination; and\par
(f) Of those complaints withdrawn by the reporting individual, the number of complaints withdrawn before the agency began an investigation as part of such agency\rquote s official discrimination claim process and the number of complaints withdrawn after such investigation began;\par
2. The number of reporting individuals, disaggregated by each reporting individual\rquote s relationship to the agency, including, but not limited to, job and internship applicant, full-time and part-time employee, intern, employee, independent contractor, and volunteer; and\par
3. Of the sexual harassment complaints supported by a preponderance of the evidence as determined by the agency, any remedial outcome, disaggregated by type of response including, but not limited to, training, demotion, change in role, suspension, and termination. The agency shall update the complaint record with the final disposition of the remedial outcome within 30 days of the date on which a final disposition is rendered.\par
\ulnone [c.] \ul d.\ulnone  The information required pursuant to [subdivision] \ul subdivisions\ulnone  b \ul and c\ulnone  of this section shall be disaggregated by agency, except that agencies with 10 employees or less shall be aggregated.\par
\ul e. The information required pursuant to subdivision c of this section shall be required to be reported except where such information was not collected before December 31, 2026.\par
\ulnone [d.] \ul f.\ulnone  No report required pursuant to [subdivision] \ul subdivisions\ulnone  b \ul and c\ulnone  of this section shall contain personally identifiable information. If any category requested contains between [0] \ul 1\ulnone  and 5 incidents of sexual harassment claims, the number shall be replaced with a symbol.\par
\'a7 3. Local law number 101 for the year 2018 is REPEALED.\i\par
\i0\'a7 4. Chapter 35 of the New York city charter is amended by adding a new section 815.4 to read as follows:\par
\ul\'a7 815.4. Workplace climate survey and agency action plans. a. Definitions. For purposes of this section, the following terms have the following meanings:\par
Covered individual. The term \ldblquote covered individual\rdblquote  means employees; interns; volunteers; contractors, subcontractors, vendors, consultants, and those they employ, who are employed by or assigned to an agency, whether temporary, seasonal, part time, or short term.\par
EEO policy. The term \ldblquote EEO policy\rdblquote  means the city\rquote s equal employment opportunity policy issued by the department.\par
b. The department shall develop and maintain a climate survey to assess covered individuals\rquote  general awareness and knowledge of the EEO policy, including, but not limited to, sexual harassment policies and prevention at agencies, including experience with and knowledge of reporting of prohibited acts. In addition, such survey shall include questions, that may be completed in full or in part, at the discretion of the covered individual completing such survey, including race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, and age of the covered individual. The department shall use such survey to assess each agency regarding the following:\par
1. The extent that covered individuals of each agency are familiar with the EEO policy;\par
2. The extent that covered individuals are knowledgeable about the EEO policy and where they can get help if they believe that they were sexually harassed;\par
3. The extent that covered individuals are knowledgeable about how and where to file a formal complaint about a violation of the EEO policy, including, but not limited to, a complaint about sexual harassment or related misconduct or how to initiate a disciplinary procedure;\par
4. The extent that covered individuals are knowledgeable about the process that occurs after a covered individual has filed a complaint about a violation of the EEO policy;\par
5. For supervisory and managerial employees, the extent that such employees are knowledgeable about their responsibilities with respect to the prevention of violations of the EEO policy, including, but not limited to, sexual harassment and retaliation as such conduct is prohibited by the city\rquote s human rights law;\par
6. For supervisory and managerial employees, the extent that such employees are knowledgeable about measures that such employees may take to appropriately address complaints under the EEO policy;\par
7. Whether covered individuals have witnessed or experienced sexual harassment, as described by local law or a violation of the EEO policy, including, but not limited to, unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favors, and other verbal or physical harassment of a sexual nature, occurring in any work\u8209?related context, such as the workplace, remote or virtual work settings, employer\u8209?sanctioned events, or any location where covered individuals are engaged in activities connected to their employment;\par
8. Whether covered individuals feel that their workplace is safe and free from violations of the EEO policy;\par
9. Whether covered individuals believe that the agency they are employed by or assigned to protects the rights of covered individuals to pursue their duties in a respectful workplace;\par
10. Whether covered individuals believe that the agency they are employed by or assigned to ensures that all covered individuals are protected from workplace harassment and ensures that all covered individuals are treated equally and fairly;\par
11. Whether covered individuals believe that the agency they are employed by or assigned to takes steps to prevent violations of the EEO policy;\par
12. Whether covered individuals believe that the agency they are employed by or assigned to takes seriously and investigates violations of the EEO policy, including, but not limited to, claims of sexual harassment; and\par
13. Whether covered individuals believe that the agency they are employed by or assigned to adequately responds to those who claim to have experienced violations of the EEO policy, including those who may be victims of sexual harassment, and ensures that appropriate resources are made available to those individuals.\par
c. The department shall make the climate survey required pursuant to subdivision b of this section available to all agencies. Agencies shall disseminate such climate survey to covered individuals and advise them that such climate survey is not mandatory or required as part of such individual\rquote s role. Agencies shall take steps to keep the assessment anonymous so that no covered individual is personally identified.\par
d. Each agency shall distribute the climate survey required by subdivision b of this section to each covered individual on or before July 31, 2028, and on or before July 31 every 4 years thereafter, and shall review the results of each climate survey in comparison to previous results of the climate survey. Each agency shall develop an action plan to identify any issues at such agency identified by the climate survey and outline what steps such agency will take to address and cure those issues and report such action plan in the annual EEO plan required pursuant to section 815.\par
e. The department shall submit a report to the mayor and the speaker of the council with the results of the climate survey prepared pursuant to subdivision b of this section on or before December 31, 2029, and on or before December 31 every 4 years thereafter for every subsequent climate survey distributed pursuant to subdivision b. The report shall include the following information:\par
\pard\ltrpar\sl480\slmult1\qj\ulnone\tab\ul 1. The number of covered individuals invited to complete the survey and the number of covered individuals who completed such survey, disaggregated by agency;\par
\ulnone\tab\ul 2. The positions of the covered individuals who completed the survey, disaggregated by type, including, but not limited to, supervisory, managerial and non-managerial; and\par
\ulnone\tab\ul 3. The work location of the covered individuals who completed a survey, disaggregated by type, including, but not limited to,\i  \i0 remote work, in-person work, and hybrid work, if such information is available; and\par
\ulnone\tab\ul 4. The agencies who created an incentive for covered individuals to complete the survey, disaggregated by type of incentive.\par
\pard\ltrpar\fi720\sl480\slmult1\qj\ulnone\'a7 4. This local law takes effect 90 days after it becomes law.\ul\par
